title: Generate All Permission Combinations
real_world_story: An access-control system has a small set of optional permissions that can be enabled or disabled independently. The system needs to generate every possible combination of these permissions.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Power Set generation where every element can either be included or excluded

problem_statement: Given N distinct permission IDs, generate all possible subsets of those permissions. Each permission may either be included or excluded from a configuration. Print the total number of possible configurations.
task: Determine the number of possible permission configurations for the given set of distinct permissions.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated distinct permission IDs.
output_format: Print the number of subsets in the power set.

examples.explanation: Three independent permissions produce 2^3 = 8 possible configurations.

expected_algorithm.name: Power Set
expected_algorithm.reason: Each permission has two choices, included or excluded, so N permissions produce 2^N possible configurations.

hint: Each permission has two possible states: selected or not selected.
The number of possible subsets doubles whenever another permission is added.
Use the relationship between subsets and powers of two.
For N permissions, the power set contains 2^N subsets.
real_world_takeaway: Power-set reasoning helps access-control systems understand how many possible permission configurations can be created from a set of independent permissions.
